Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 38006 of 2024

Applicant :- Idrish Ahmad
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Anand Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Anand Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.N. Srivastava, learned
Aga, for the State.

2.  The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.10 of 2024, under Sections 364, 302, 201 I.P.C., Police Station Kanth,
District Moradabad, during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged by the applicant himself on 19.01.2024 under Section 363 IPC and according to the FIR, on 18.01.2024 at about 10:00 am, the son of the applicant aged about 7 years had gone somewhere from his house and thereafter, he could not be traced.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that it is a case, in which, informant i.e. applicant during investigation has been made accused.

sentences.text:
He further submits, FIR of the present case was lodged by the applicant himself with regard to the missing of his step son but after lodging the FIR, when second wife of the applicant i.e. mother of the missing boy moved an application that applicant is the step father of her son Hasan and she is having doubt that she concealed him somewhere then thereafter, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.
6.

He further submits that as per prosecution, when applicant was arrested then he confessed his guilt and on his pointing out the dead body of his step son was recovered from an open place i.e.
road.

7. He next submits that entire allegation levelled against the applicant is false and as mother of the deceased was second wife of the applicant and deceased was not the son of the applicant, therefore,
she was having suspicion that applicant did not like him and therefore, during investigation, she started making allegation against the applicant.

8. He further submits, as recovery of the dead body of the deceased was made from an open place accessible to all, therefore, only on the basis of recovery, at this stage, it cannot be said that applicant committed the murder of his step son.

9. He next submits, except the confessional statement of the applicant and recovery of the body of the deceased on his pointing out and allegation levelled by his second wife i.e. mother of the deceased, there is no other evidence against the applicant on record.

10. He next submits, admittedly, nobody could witness that applicant committed the murder of the deceased and it is a case of circumstantial evidence and chain of circumstances could not be completed.
11.

He next submits, however, apart from the present case, applicant is having criminal history of six cases but four cases were of minor offences and however, one case was of Section 302 IPC but in that case, applicant has already been acquitted and in case under Section 376 IPC, he is on bail.
12. He further submits, in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 25.01.2024 i.e. for last almost ten months.

13. Per contra, learned AGA however opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that from the statement of the mother of the deceased, who is also second wife of the applicant, it reflects that according to her, deceased had gone along with applicant and thereafter, he did not return and after five days his dead body was recovered on the pointing out of the applicant but could not dispute the fact that applicant was the informant of the case and mother of the deceased resided along with the applicant and she moved an application on 24.01.2024 against the applicant i.e. after five days after recovery of the dead body and at the time of lodgment of the FIR, she did not raise any objection against the applicant.

sentences.text:
Learned AGA further, could not dispute the fact that even except the evidence of last seen given by the mother of the deceased and confessional statement of the applicant and recovery of the dead body on the pointing out of the applicant, there is no other evidence against the applicant on record.
15.
He further could not dispute the fact that dead body was recovered from an open place.
16. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

17. It is a case of circumstantial evidence and applicant was the person, who lodged FIR of the present case with regard to the missing of his step son but during investigation when after five days from the date of lodgment of the FIR, his second wife moved an application against the applicant that he is the culprit, then he made accused in the present matter.
18. Further, however, on the pointing out of the applicant, as per allegation, dead body of the deceased was recovered but it reflects that recovery was made from an open place accessible to all.

19. Further, however, second wife of the applicant i.e. mother of the deceased stated in her statement recorded during investigation and in her application that deceased had gone along with applicant but this disclosure was made by her after five days and at the time of the lodgment of the FIR by the applicant, she did not disclose this fact to anyone including police.

20. Further, however apart from the present case, applicant is having criminal history of six cases including case of Section 302 IPC but in that case, it reflects, he has already acquitted and in a case under Section 376 IPC, he is on bail and all the other cases relate to minor offences.
21.
Further, law is settled, if otherwise, case of bail is made out then merely on the basis of criminal antecedents of accused, ordinarily, bail application should not be withheld.
22. Further, in the present matter, applicant is in jail since 25.01.2024 i.e. for last almost 10 months 23.

Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
24. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

25. Let the applicant- Idrish Ahmad be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
26. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

27. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
